cluster_name: Ukraine drone campaign strikes Wildberries warehouses across Russia
event_summary: Ukrainian drones struck Wildberries warehouses near Moscow, St. Petersburg, and Tver on August 4, killing at least five people and injuring ten. Ukraine has targeted the e-commerce giant since July 18, claiming its warehouses supply drone components to Russia's military.
tldr: Headlines across all eleven outlet buckets lead with drone-strike kill counts and warehouse fires, making SECURITY_DEFENSE the near-universal advertised frame at the homepage level. Only two outlets break from this register at the title level: Meduza (exiled Russian press) makes the economic dimension headline-visible by naming 215–280 billion rubles in seller losses, while The Independent deploys the ‘Russian Amazon’ consumer metaphor to signal Wildberries’ civilian-commercial character. RFE/RL is the sole outlet whose headline surfaces a policy frame, tying the strikes to Zelenskyy’s demand for faster Patriot deliveries. Kyiv Post is unique in framing Ukraine’s campaign as capacity degradation at the title level — naming a drone-development university and logistics hubs as targets — while Daily Sabah inverts the cluster’s dominant framing direction entirely, leading with Russia’s missile attack on Kyiv.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only title in the cluster to foreground Russia's offensive strike on Kyiv ('Russia launches massive missile, drone attack on Kyiv, 9 dead') rather than Ukraine's Wildberries campaign, inverting the cluster's dominant framing direction at homepage level.

The only headline to quantify the financial scale of the campaign in rubles ('Forbes Russia: Wildberries sellers’ losses… estimated at 215–280 billion rubles'), making the economic dimension of the crisis headline-visible where every other outlet reduces the story to military action.

The only title to explicitly flag evidentiary uncertainty about Ukraine’s justification for targeting Wildberries — 'Ukraine says online retail giant Wildberries helps supply Russia’s military. Meduza examines the evidence.' — surfacing the legitimacy dispute at homepage level.

The only title to lead with Russia’s air-defense performance ('Russia downs 320 drones') rather than Ukraine’s strike operation, framing Russia as the active defensive agent and subordinating the kill count to the air-defense achievement.

The only outlet to deploy the ‘Russian Amazon’ consumer metaphor in its headline, making Wildberries’ civilian-commercial identity — and the dual-use tension at the heart of the story — explicitly homepage-visible.

The only outlet to name a Russian drone-development university as a strike target in its headline, expanding the headline-visible scope of Ukraine’s campaign beyond commercial logistics to military R&D infrastructure.

bottom_line: The headline layer compresses a multi-dimensional story into a near-uniform SECURITY_DEFENSE register — kill counts and warehouse fires dominate homepage framing across all eleven outlet buckets — while the economic fallout, the legitimacy dispute over targeting a civilian retailer, and Ukraine’s capacity-degradation rationale remain almost entirely headline-invisible, surfaced only by Meduza’s rubles figure and The Independent’s ‘Russian Amazon’ label.
